paragraphs: SunCoke Energy, Inc. ("SunCoke Energy," "SunCoke," "Company," "we," "our" and "us") is the largest independent producer of high-quality coke in the Americas, as measured by tons of coke produced each year, and has more than 65 years of coke production experience. Coke is produced by heating metallurgical coal in a refractory oven, which releases certain volatile components from the coal, thus transforming the coal into coke. Our coke is primarily used as a principal raw material in the blast furnace steelmaking process as well as in the foundry production of casted iron, and the majority of our sales are derived from blast furnace coke sales made under long-term, take-or-pay agreements. We also sell coke produced utilizing capacity in excess of that reserved for our long-term, take-or-pay agreements to customers in both the export and North American domestic coke markets seeking high-quality product for their blast furnaces. We have designed, developed and built, and we currently own and operate five cokemaking facilities in the United States ("U.S.") with collective nameplate capacity to produce approximately 3.7 million tons of blast furnace coke per year. Additionally, we designed and currently operate one cokemaking facility in Brazil under licensing and operating agreements on behalf of ArcelorMittal Brasil S.A. ("ArcelorMittal Brazil"), which has approximately 1.7 million tons of annual cokemaking capacity.

We also own and operate an industrial services business that provides export and domestic material handling and/or mixing services to coke, coal, steel, power and other bulk customers, as well as mission-critical mill services to leading steel producers globally. Our logistics terminals have the collective capacity to mix and transload more than 40 million tons of coal and other products annually and have storage capacity of approximately 3 million tons. These terminals are strategically located to reach Gulf Coast, East Coast, Great Lakes and international ports. Industrial services also include the removal, handling, and processing of molten slag at customer sites, as well as preparation and transportation of metal scraps, raw materials, and finished products.
We report our business results through two reportable segments: Domestic Coke and Industrial Services.

Our Domestic Coke segment consists of cokemaking facilities and heat recovery operations at our Jewell, Indiana Harbor, Haverhill, Granite City and Middletown plants. Our core business model is predicated on providing steelmakers an alternative to investing capital in their own captive coke production facilities and to serve as the long-term supplier of high quality coke by investing in our facilities with leading technology, as well as safety and environmental performance. Our cokemaking ovens utilize efficient, modern heat recovery technology designed to combust the coal's volatile components during the cokemaking process and use the hot flue gas to generate steam and electricity for sale through steam generation facilities or cogeneration plants, respectively. This differs from by-product cokemaking, which repurposes the coal's volatile components for other uses. Steam generated is generally sold to customers pursuant to steam supply and purchase agreements, and electricity generated is generally sold into the regional power market or to customers pursuant to energy sales agreements.

We believe our advanced heat recovery cokemaking process has numerous advantages over by-product cokemaking, including producing higher quality coke, using waste heat to generate derivative energy for resale, and reducing the environmental footprint. The Clean Air Act Amendments of 1990 specifically directed the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency ("EPA") to evaluate our heat recovery coke oven technology as a basis for establishing Maximum Achievable Control Technology ("MACT") standards for new cokemaking facilities. In addition, each of the four cokemaking facilities that we have built since 1990 has either met or exceeded the applicable Best Available Control Technology ("BACT"), or Lowest Achievable Emission Rate ("LAER") standards, as applicable, set forth by the EPA for cokemaking facilities. We have constructed the only greenfield cokemaking facilities in the U.S. in over 35 years and are the only North American coke producer that utilizes heat recovery technology in the cokemaking process.

headings: Risks Inherent in Our Business and Industry

paragraphs: Our business, operating results, cash flows and financial condition are subject to these risks and uncertainties, any of

which could cause actual results to vary materially and adversely from recent results or from anticipated future results. In addition to the other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and in our other filings with the SEC, the following risk factors should be considered in evaluating our business and future prospects.
These risk factors represent what we believe to be the known material risk factors with respect to us and our business.

However, these are not the only risks we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us, or that we currently deem to be immaterial also may materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, or results of operations.

Our cokemaking and industrial services businesses are subject to operating risks, some of which are beyond our control. Equipment failures or deterioration of assets, may lead to major incidents, production curtailments, shutdowns, impairments, or additional expenditures, which could materially and adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition.

Factors beyond our control could disrupt our cokemaking and industrial services operations, adversely affect our ability to service the needs of our customers and increase our operating costs, all of which could have a material and adverse effect on our results of operations. Adverse developments at our cokemaking facilities could significantly disrupt our ability to produce and supply coke, steam, and/or energy to our customers. Adverse developments at our industrial services operations could significantly disrupt our ability to provide scrap handling and sales, slag handling and sales, metals recovery, labor, handling, mixing, storage, terminalling, transloading and/or transportation services, of coal and other dry and liquid bulk commodities, to our customers. Our operations depend upon critical pieces of equipment that occasionally may be out of service for scheduled upgrades or maintenance or as a result of unanticipated failures. Assets and equipment critical to these operations also may deteriorate or become depleted materially sooner than we currently estimate, resulting in additional maintenance spending or additional timely replacement capital expenditures.

paragraphs: •One Big Beautiful Bill Act. On July 4, 2025, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act ("OBBBA") was enacted into law. The OBBBA includes significant provisions, such as the permanent extension of certain expiring provisions of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, modifications to the international tax framework and the restoration of favorable tax treatment for certain business provisions. The legislation has multiple effective dates, with certain provisions effective in 2025 and others implemented through 2027. Following the enactment of the OBBBA, the Company recognized the tax effects of the legislation in the interim period that included the enactment date, as required under ASC 740, Income Taxes. The Company has evaluated the impact of the OBBBA on cash taxes, deferred tax assets and liabilities and has reflected these effects in the consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2025.

•Revolving Facility Extension. On July 25, 2025, we amended and extended the maturity of our revolving credit facility ("Revolving Facility") to July 2030 under substantially similar terms. The amendment also reduced the Revolving Facility capacity by $25.0 million to $325.0 million.

•Acquisition of Phoenix Global. On August 1, 2025, we completed the acquisition of Phoenix Global, a privately held provider of mission-critical mill services to major steel producing companies. We acquired Phoenix Global for preliminary purchase consideration of $295.8 million. See Note 3 to our consolidated financial statements for further detail.

•Algoma Coke Supply Contract. At the end of the third quarter of 2025, we were notified of Algoma Steel Inc's breach of contract and refusal to accept any additional coke tons. We are actively pursuing all avenues to enforce the contract and recover any financial losses.

•Haverhill II Contract Extension. In November 2025, the Haverhill II long-term, take-or-pay agreement with Cleveland-Cliffs Steel Holding Corporation and Cleveland-Cliffs Steel LLC, subsidiaries of Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. and collectively referred to as "Cliffs Steel," was extended through December 31, 2028. Under the extension, the Company will provide 500 thousand tons of metallurgical coke annually.

•Haverhill I Closure. In the fourth quarter of 2025, the Company made the decision to optimize its coke fleet and close its Haverhill I cokemaking facility in the first quarter of 2026, resulting in the impairment charges discussed above.

•Granite City Contract Extension. In January 2026, the Granite City long-term, take-or-pay agreement with United States Steel Corporation ("U.S. Steel") was extended through December 31, 2026. Under the extension, the Company will provide 590 thousand tons of metallurgical coke. The provisions and economics of this extension remain similar to those included in the previous extensions executed in 2024 and 2025.

paragraphs: SunCoke Energy, Inc. ("SunCoke Energy," "SunCoke," "Company," "we," "our" and "us") 為美洲地區最大的獨立高品質焦炭生產商，以每年生產的焦炭噸數計算，擁有超過 65 年的焦炭生產經驗。焦炭是透過將冶金煤加熱於耐火爐中製造而成，此過程會釋放煤中的某些揮發性零組件，進而將煤轉化為焦炭。我們的焦炭主要用作高爐煉鋼過程中的主要原料，以及鑄造鐵生產，而我們銷售的大部分收入來自於根據長期買賣協議所進行的高爐焦炭銷售。我們也銷售利用超出長期買賣協議所保留容量的生產能力所製造的焦炭，供出口市場與北美地區的客戶使用，這些客戶尋求高品質的產品用於其高爐。我們已設計、開發並建造，目前擁有並營運五座位於美國（"U.S.") 的焦炭生產設施，總共的名義產能為每年生產約 3.7 百萬噸的高爐焦炭。此外，我們設計並目前營運一座位於巴西的焦炭生產設施，為 ArcelorMittal Brasil S.A. ("ArcelorMittal Brazil") 依照授權與營運協議所進行，該設施的年焦炭生產能力約為 1.7 百萬噸。

我們也擁有並營運一個工業服務業務，為焦炭、煤炭、鋼鐵、電力及其他大宗貨物客戶提供出口與國內的物料處理及/或混合服務，同時也為全球主要鋼鐵生產商提供關鍵性磨坊服務。我們的物流碼頭總共的混合與轉運能力為每年超過 40 百萬噸的煤炭及其他產品，並擁有約 3 百萬噸的儲存空間。這些碼頭 strategically 位於美國墨西哥灣沿岸、東海岸、五大湖地區及國際港口。工業服務也包括在客戶現場移除、處理及處理熔融爐渣，以及準備與運輸金屬廢料、原料及成品。
我們透過兩個應報告分部報告業務成果：國內焦炭與工業服務。

我們的國內焦炭分部包含我們 Jewell、Indiana Harbor、Haverhill、Granite City 與 Middletown 廠區的焦炭生產設施與熱能回收作業。我們的核心業務模式是為鋼鐵廠提供一個替代方案，使其無需投資於自有焦炭生產設施，並作為長期供應高品質焦炭的供應商，透過投資於具備領先技術、安全與環境表現的設施。我們的焦炭生產爐使用高效能、現代化的熱能回收技術，在焦炭生產過程中燃燒煤的揮發性零組件，並利用熱煙氣產生蒸汽與電力，供應至蒸汽發電設施或 cogeneration 廠區。這與副產品焦炭生產不同，後者會將煤的揮發性零組件重新利用於其他用途。產生的蒸汽通常根據蒸汽供應與購買協議出售給客戶，產生的電力則通常出售至區域電力市場或根據能源銷售協議出售給客戶。

我們相信我們先進的熱能回收焦炭生產過程相比副產品焦炭生產有許多優勢，包括生產更高品質的焦炭、利用廢熱產生衍生能源進行銷售，以及減少環境足跡。1990 年潔淨空氣法案修正案特別指示美國環境保護署（"EPA"）評估我們的熱能回收焦炭爐技術，作為建立新焦炭生產設施 Maximum Achievable Control Technology（"MACT"）標準的基礎。此外，我們自 1990 年以來建造的四座焦炭生產設施，均已符合或超越 EPA 所設定的 Best Available Control Technology（"BACT"）或 Lowest Achievable Emission Rate（"LAER"）標準。我們建造了美國 35 年來唯一的全新焦炭生產設施，並是唯一在焦炭生產過程中使用熱能回收技術的北美焦炭生產商。

paragraphs: •一項重大美好法案。於 2025 年 7 月 4 日，一項重大美好法案（"OBBBA"）已成為法律。OBBBA 包含重要條款，例如永久延長某些即將到期的《減稅與就業法案》條款、修改國際稅收架構以及恢復某些商業條款的有利稅收待遇。該法案有多個生效日期，部分條款於 2025 年生效，其他則於 2027 年實施。OBBBA 頒佈後，本公司於包含頒佈日期的中間期間認列該法案的稅務影響，如 ASC 740，收入稅所述。本公司已評估 OBBBA 對現金稅、遞延稅資產與負債的影響，並已反映這些影響於 2025 年 12 月 31 日結止之合併財務報表中。
•循環信貸融資協議延長。於 2025 年 7 月 25 日，本公司修改並延長循環信貸融資協議（"循環信貸融資"）的到期日至 2030 年 7 月，條款與先前 substantially similar。修改同時將循環信貸融資額度減少 25.0 百萬美元至 325.0 百萬美元。
•收購 Phoenix Global。於 2025 年 8 月 1 日，本公司完成收購 Phoenix Global，一家 privately held 提供關鍵性 mill 服務給主要鋼鐵生產公司的企業。本公司以初步買方對價 295.8 百萬美元收購 Phoenix Global。有關更多細節，請參閱我們合併財務報表的附註 3。
•Algoma 焦炭供應契約。於 2025 年第三季末，本公司得知 Algoma Steel Inc 違約並拒絕接受任何額外焦炭噸數。本公司正積極追尋所有途徑以執行契約並彌補任何財務損失。

•Haverhill II 契約延長。於 2025 年 11 月，本公司與 Cleveland-Cliffs Steel Holding Corporation 和 Cleveland-Cliffs Steel LLC（Cleveland-Cliffs Inc 的子公司， collectively 稱為 "Cliffs Steel"）之間的 Haverhill II 長期、take-or-pay 契約已延長至 2028 年 12 月 31 日。根據延長契約，本公司將每年提供 500 千噸冶金焦炭。
•Haverhill I 停產。於 2025 年第四季，本公司決定優化其焦炭船隊並於 2026 年第一季關閉 Haverhill I 焦炭製造廠，導致上述所討論的減損費用。

•Granite City 契約延長。於 2026 年 1 月，本公司與 United States Steel Corporation（"U.S. Steel"）之間的 Granite City 長期、take-or-pay 契約已延長至 2026 年 12 月 31 日。根據延長契約，本公司將提供 590 千噸冶金焦炭。此延長契約的條款與經濟效益與 2024 年及 2025 年執行的先前延長契約相似。

headings: 長期資產帳面價值減損可能對我們的營運、財務狀況及營業成果造成重大且不利的影響。
我們的營運可能影響環境或導致暴露於有害污染物，這可能會對我們產生重大負債。
對永續議題的利害關係人監督可能對我們的營運及股票價格造成重大且不利的影響。
與我們的煉焦業務相關的風險
若我們無法在煉焦設施維持有效的品質控制系統，可能對我們的營業成果造成重大不利影響。
若我們無法有效保護我們的智慧財產權，第三方可能使用我們的技術，這將影響我們在市場中的競爭能力。
與我們的工業服務業務相關的風險
負債、流動性及財務狀況相關風險
本公司可能面臨重大債務到期，可能不利於整體財務狀況。
本公司可能因通貨膨脹的影響而受到不利影響。
paragraphs: 本公司營運、營運成果、現金流及財務狀況受這些風險與不確定性影響，任何一項都可能使實際結果與近期結果或預期未來結果有重大且不利的差異。
除本年度10-K表報表及其他向SEC提交的文件中所包含的資訊外，在評估本公司營運及未來展望時，應考慮下列風險因素。
這些風險因素代表本公司認為與本公司及營運有關的已知重大風險因素。
然而，這些並非我們唯一面臨的風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為我們所知，或目前我們認為不重要，但這些風險與不確定性仍可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。
本公司之煉焦與工業服務業務面臨營運風險，其中部分風險超出我們的控制範圍。設備故障或資產劣化，可能導致重大事故、生產減少、停機、減損或額外支出，這些情況可能對我們的營運成果與財務狀況產生重大且不利的影響。

超出我們控制範圍的因素可能幹擾我們的煉焦與工業服務業務運作，不利於我們服務客戶的能力，並提高我們的營運成本，所有這些情況都可能對我們的營運成果產生重大且不利的影響。本公司煉焦設施若發生不利發展，可能顯著幹擾我們向客戶生產與供應焦炭、蒸汽及/或能源的能力。本公司工業服務業務若發生不利發展，可能顯著幹擾我們向客戶提供廢鋼處理與銷售、爐渣處理與銷售、金屬回收、勞務、處理、混合、儲存、碼頭、轉運及/或運輸煤及其他乾燥與液態散裝貨物服務的能力。本公司運作依賴關鍵性設備，這些設備偶爾可能因預定升級或維護而無法運作，或因未預期的故障而無法運作。這些運作所依賴的資產與設備，也可能比我們目前預估更早劣化或耗盡，導致額外的維護支出或額外的及時更換資本支出。
